title: Combination of outpatient psychotherapy and online modules for patients with somatic symptom disorder (iSOMA+): Effects of blended psychotherapy
summary:
Many people experience so-called persistent physical symptoms such as pain, fatigue, or digestive problems. These symptoms can follow medical illnesses, stressful life events, or due to high stress levels. Often, a combination of different risk factors plays a role. Sometimes, the physical complaints cannot be fully explained by medical findings. If these symptoms persist over a longer period, cause significant distress, and interfere with daily life, this is referred to as a somatic symptom disorder. A key feature of this condition is that affected individuals often worry excessively about their symptoms, frequently seek medical care, or avoid certain activities out of fear that their symptoms might worsen. These behaviors can, in turn, worsen the symptoms and reduce quality of life.
To relieve symptoms and improve how people manage their condition, medical guidelines recommend not only appropriate medical care but also psychological treatment. One type of therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), has proven to be effective. However, the effects of psychotherapy on long-lasting physical symptoms are still limited, so there is a need for new and innovative treatment approaches.
A promising new approach is called Blended Care – a combination of in-person therapy sessions and digital tools (such as exercises or materials) that patients can use on their own. In our study, we are testing whether this type of support can improve the effects of outpatient psychotherapy for people with persistent physical symptoms who meet the criteria for somatic symptom disorder.
In the study, we compare two forms of treatment:
Blended Care (20 sessions individual psychotherapy + 7 modules in online program)
Standard Treatment (20 sessions individual psychotherapy + self-help guide)

The goal of the study is to find out whether Blended Care reduces physical symptoms and related distress and limitations more effectively than standard treatment, and whether these improvements last for up to six months after therapy has ended.

The duration of treatment per patient is approximately six months. A total of 250 patients will take part in the study at eight outpatient psychotherapy clinics across Germany.

interventions.name: Blended Care, consisting of individual psychotherapy (20 sessions) + online intervention (7 modules), approx. 6 months treatment duration)
Standard treatment, consisting of individual psychotherapy  (20 sessions) + self-help booklet, approx. 6 months treatment duration

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Main diagnosis of Somatic Symptom Disorder according to DSM-5 via DIPS
2) Sufficient level of symptom severity in the Patient Health Questionnaire, somatic symptom version (PHQ-15 ≥ 5)
3) Disability in an adapted version of the Pain Disability Inventory (PDI ≥ 4)
4) Private internet-access and an internet-capable device
5) Signed "informed consent"
Exclusion criteria:
1) Any acute, severe, or unstable physical condition (e.g., organic brain disorders, severe cognitive deficits) that does not allow for safe participa-tion based on the patient's self-reports, existing medical documentation (including consultation report)
2) Insufficient German reading and/or language skills
3) Substance use disorders
4) Acute psychotic state
5) Acute suicidality
6) Parallel psychological treatment 
7) Parallel participation in another intervention study
